name: post-decisions
prompt: help me submit a talk to the local Go meetup, they want a short abstract and a bio
note: Two decisions (whether to name the employer, 'your call'; keep or drop the benchmark chart) and two actions (confirm the slot length with the organizers; check the bio photo link). min 2 leaves room for the two checks to come back as one item.
message:
Here's a draft you can paste into the form.

**Title:** Shrinking a Go service's memory by 70% without a rewrite

**Abstract (148 words):** Our billing service grew from 300 MB to 2 GB of memory over a year, and nobody had changed anything big. This talk walks through how we found where the memory went using only the standard library's profiler, why the biggest win was a three-line change to how we reuse buffers, and which "obvious" fixes made things worse. You'll leave with a checklist you can run against your own service in an afternoon. No prior profiling experience needed.

**Bio:** Backend engineer who spends too much time reading heap profiles. Based in town, usually at the back of the room with a laptop open.

Two things are up to you:
1. **Naming your employer.** The story is more credible with the company name in it, but some companies want to approve talks first. It's your call whether to add it.
2. **The memory chart.** I left a placeholder for the before-and-after chart. It's the most convincing part of the abstract, but the numbers are internal. Keep it, or drop it and describe the drop in words?

Before you submit:
- **Confirm the slot length.** The form says 20 minutes, but last month's talks ran 30. Ask the organizers which one, since the abstract promises a lot for 20.
- **Check the photo link.** Your bio photo URL returned a 404 when I tried it. Upload a new one or link a different picture.
